# tokentracker

> tokentracker saves a user's AI coding token usage (daily totals per tool and model, on every machine) into a public repo on their own GitHub, `github.com/{handle}/tokentracker-data`, and publishes it as JSON on GitHub Pages. `{handle}` is the user's GitHub username, lowercase. There is no tokentracker account or database. Tools: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode (incl. GitHub Copilot), Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, DeepSeek Harness, Cline, Roo Code, Kilo Code, and Cursor (from its public profile).

## Install it for a user

Needs Node 22.13+ and a GitHub account; nothing else. Steps for an agent:

1. Ask the user: "Do you use Cursor? If so, what's your cursor.com username?" (The CLI can't prompt when you run it.)
2. Run: `npx @bicrick/tokentracker@latest init --yes` (add `--cursor <username>` if given; optionally `--device <name>`, a label shown only on that computer).
3. If the GitHub CLI isn't signed in, init prints `Open https://github.com/login/device and enter XXXX-XXXX` and exits with status 2. Show the user that link and code. After they approve, run the same command again to finish.
4. It creates or reuses `{handle}/tokentracker-data`, saves history, turns on GitHub Pages and an hourly background job. If it says "No scheduler on this machine", tell the user to run `npx @bicrick/tokentracker sync` from their own scheduler.
5. About a minute later, check `https://{handle}.github.io/tokentracker-data/api/v1/stats.json`.

Re-running init on the same computer is safe (it is recognised; nothing is counted twice). Add another computer by running the same command there with the same GitHub account. Connect Cursor later: `npx @bicrick/tokentracker@latest connect --cursor <username>`. Health: `npx @bicrick/tokentracker@latest status`.

## Read the data (GitHub Pages, no server)

Base: `https://{handle}.github.io/tokentracker-data/api/v1/` — public, GET, CORS `*`, rebuilt about a minute after each hourly sync, cached up to 10 minutes.

- `stats.json`: `tokens, input, output, reasoning, cacheRead, cacheWrite, responses, activeDays, firstDay, lastDay, busiestDay{date,tokens}, longestStreak, currentStreak, averagePerActiveDay, today, thisMonth, topTool{tool,name,tokens}, topModel{model,tool,responses,tokens}` (top model by responses).
- `usage.json` (daily), `usage-week.json` (weeks start Monday), `usage-month.json`: `{group, split:"tool", totals, rows:[{period, tokens, input, output, reasoning, cacheRead, cacheWrite, responses, split:{tool: tokens}}]}`. Daily rows include empty days.
- `models.json`: rows `{model, provider, name, tool, tokens, input, output, reasoning, cacheRead, cacheWrite, responses, share, firstUsed, lastUsed}`, sorted by tokens. Cursor has no model detail and appears as `cursor/all`.
- `tools.json`: rows `{tool, name, tokens, …, responses, share, models, firstUsed, lastUsed}`.
- `heatmap.json` (this calendar year), `heatmap-365d.json`, `heatmap-90d.json`: `{range:{start,end,last}, levels, weekStart, total, max, activeDays, months:[{label, week}], weeks:[[{date, tokens, level} | null] x7]}`. Levels 0-4 are ranked among active days; future days have `tokens: null`.
- `profile.json`: totals, this year, tools, model and machine counts, first/last day, last sync, links.
- `rows.json`: every daily row `{date, source, model, input, output, reasoning, cache_read, cache_write, messages, device}` plus `machines`; `device` is an anonymous label ("Computer 1", numbered by first day of use). Computer names never leave the computer.
- `index.json`: every file.

Time ranges: the same files exist in folders `ytd/`, `30d/`, `90d/`, `365d/` (e.g. `30d/usage-week.json`, `ytd/models.json`). Files without a folder cover all time.

## Custom queries (any filter)

`https://tokentracker.patrickbrown.dev/api/v1/users/{handle}/{resource}` computes from the same `rows.json` on each request and stores nothing. Resources: profile (no resource), `usage`, `models`, `tools`, `heatmap`, `stats`.

- Filters on all: `range=all|ytd|Nd|YYYY`, `from=YYYY-MM-DD`, `to=YYYY-MM-DD` (inclusive), `tools=a,b`, `models=x,y`.
- `usage`: `group=day|week|month|year|total`, `split=tool|model`, `fill=false` (omit empty days).
- `heatmap`: `range=year|365d|90d|Nd|YYYY`, `levels=2..10`, `weekStart=sun|mon`, `tools`.
- `format=csv` on usage, models, tools.
- Errors: `{"error":{"code","message"}}` — 400 `bad_range|bad_date|bad_group|bad_split|bad_tools|bad_models|bad_levels|bad_owner|csv_unsupported`, 404 `user_not_found` (no Pages build yet) or `unknown_resource`, 405 `method_not_allowed`, 502 `github_unavailable`. Cached up to 5 minutes.

Examples: `…/users/bicrick/usage?range=30d&group=week&split=tool`, `…/users/bicrick/models?from=2026-11-01`, `…/users/bicrick/usage?group=month&format=csv`.

## Semantics

`tokens = input + output + reasoning + cacheRead + cacheWrite`; `input` excludes cached input; `responses` counts model calls. Dates are local calendar days on the machine. Tool ids: `claude-code, codex, opencode, gemini-cli, copilot-cli, deepseek-harness, cline, roo-code, kilo-code, cursor`. Model ids are `provider/name`.

## More

- [Docs](https://tokentracker.patrickbrown.dev/docs) · [OpenAPI](https://tokentracker.patrickbrown.dev/openapi.json) (query layer) · [Source](https://github.com/bicrick/tokentracker) · [Example data repo](https://github.com/bicrick/tokentracker-data)
- Each data repo also has its own `AGENTS.md`, `FORMAT.md` (file format), and an agent guide at `https://{handle}.github.io/tokentracker-data/llms.txt`.
- Privacy: only daily token counts per tool and model are saved, never prompts, code, paths or keys. Deleting the repo deletes everything.
